title.en: Economics: Understanding Development: Perspectives, Measurement and Sustainability

text.en: Asha asked why some countries seem richer than others. "That is development," said her teacher.

Development means improvement in people's lives. It is not only growth in income but also better health, education and living conditions. Different people may have different ideas of development.
Per capita income is the total income divided by the population. The Human Development Index (HDI) measures life expectancy, education and income, and countries are ranked by it. The Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is the value of goods and services produced.
Sustainable development meets present needs without damaging the resources for the future. The Sustainable Development Goals set by the UN include ending poverty and hunger, and giving quality education.
Development means improvement in people's lives.
It is not only growth in income but also better health, education and living conditions.
Different people may have different ideas of development.
Per capita income is the total income divided by the population.
The Human Development Index (HDI) measures life expectancy, education and income, and countries are ranked by it.
The Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is the value of goods and services produced.
Sustainable development meets present needs without damaging the resources for the future.
The Sustainable Development Goals set by the UN include ending poverty and hunger, and giving quality education.
Different people have different development goals. A landless farm labourer wants steady work and fair wages, whereas an industrialist may want reliable electricity and smooth highways.
Sometimes goals even conflict: building a large dam brings irrigation and electricity to farmers and cities, but it can submerge forest villages and displace tribal families.
Because people want more than income—such as respect, safety, clean air, freedom and good schools—economists look at both income and non-income indicators.
Let us examine the main economic indicators. Net National Product, or NNP, measures the total value of final goods and services produced by a nation's citizens after deducting depreciation.
Per Capita Income equals total national income divided by total population. It shows average income per person, making it easy to compare small and large countries.
However, an average hides inequality. If one person earns ninety thousand rupees and nine earn almost nothing, the average looks decent even though most people remain poor.
Purchasing Power Parity, or PPP, compares how much a basket of everyday goods actually costs in different countries, giving a fairer view of real living standards.
To capture human well-being beyond money, the United Nations Development Programme publishes the Human Development Index, or HDI.
HDI combines three core dimensions: a long and healthy life measured by life expectancy, knowledge measured by years of schooling, and a decent standard of living measured by GNI per capita.
Other vital social indicators include Literacy Rate—the percentage of people aged seven and above who can read and write with understanding—and Net Attendance Ratio in schools.
Health progress is tracked through Infant Mortality Rate, life expectancy at birth, and access to clean drinking water and sanitation.
Public facilities matter enormously because money in one family's pocket cannot buy a pollution-free city, herd immunity from vaccines, or a clean public river.
Tamil Nadu and Kerala score strongly on literacy, public healthcare and noon-meal nutrition compared with several states that have similar or higher average incomes.

board.text: Strong social investment in TN & Kerala

text.en: Now let us turn to sustainability. Sustainable development means meeting the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.
Natural resources fall into two groups: renewable resources like sunlight, wind and replenished groundwater, and non-renewable resources like coal, petroleum and mineral ores.
Even renewable resources can be exhausted if we use them faster than nature refills them—for example, pumping borewells far faster than monsoon rain recharges aquifers.
Non-renewable fossil fuels formed over millions of years. Once burned, they cannot be replaced quickly and release greenhouse gases that warm the planet.

board.text: Fossil fuels are finite & warm climate

text.en: India's environmental laws—such as the Wildlife Protection Act, Forest Conservation Act and Environment Protection Act—guard forests, rivers and clean air.
Tamil Nadu is a national leader in renewable energy, generating large shares of power from wind turbines in Muppandal and Aralvaimozhi and from expanding solar parks.

board.text: Tamil Nadu leads in wind & solar power

text.en: Simple community choices—rainwater harvesting, public transit, solar rooftops and cutting single-use plastics—turn sustainability from a slogan into daily practice.
To evaluate any state or nation fairly, never stop at GDP alone: check Per Capita Income, HDI, literacy, health and resource sustainability together.
True development lifts every citizen's health, knowledge and dignity while keeping Earth's water, soil and climate healthy for children yet to come.

problem.en: State A has higher Per Capita Income than State B, but State B has higher literacy, longer life expectancy and lower infant mortality. Which state has stronger human development?

text.en: Compare income versus human well-being indicators.

why.en: State A leads in average income, while State B leads in education and health outcomes.

text.en: Apply the Human Development Index framework.

why.en: HDI weighs health and education alongside income because money alone does not guarantee schools, clinics or clean water.

text.en: Draw the conclusion.

why.en: State B shows stronger human development; State A needs to invest more of its income in public healthcare and education.

prompt.en: A friend says Development means only more income. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: It also means health and education.
